Start with an input file from the maintained OPALX regression suite. Those
inputs are executable specifications and are checked continuously against the
current parser and physics implementation.

::: {.feature-opalx}

If you already have an OPAL, ASTRA or Elegant model, `toOPALX.py` can prepare
an OPALX input file. See @sec-toopalx for the download, supported inputs,
conversion commands and model-review requirements.

:::

## Run a small regression input {#regression-smoke-test}

From the root of the OPALX checkout, after building the serial executable:

```bash
export OPALX_EXE="$PWD/build_serial/src/opalx"
git clone https://github.com/OPALX-project/regression-tests-x.git
mkdir -p run-drift
cp regression-tests-x/RegressionTests/Drift-1-fromfile/Drift-1-fromfile.in run-drift/
cp regression-tests-x/RegressionTests/Drift-1-fromfile/distr-gauss.txt run-drift/
cd run-drift
"$OPALX_EXE" Drift-1-fromfile.in --info 2
```

This case tracks 1,000 electrons through a drift with self-fields disabled
(`FIELDSOLVER, TYPE=NONE`). Keep `distr-gauss.txt` beside the input: the
particle distribution is read from that file. The run writes
`Drift-1-fromfile.stat`; check that it completes successfully and produces
statistics.

This is a **smoke test**, not an automated numerical regression comparison.
The regression repository also supplies a `.rt` file defining checked metrics
and tolerances, and a `reference/` directory with reference results. See the
[regression repository]({{< meta regression-tests-source-url >}}/README.md)
for its structure and the dashboard below for current results. Do not
regenerate references merely to make a failing check pass.

The regression repository evolves independently of OPALX releases. Record its
revision with `git -C ../regression-tests-x rev-parse HEAD` when reporting a
result; its default branch is not a frozen 1.0.0 test suite.

## Launch on a GPU


For a multi-GPU run, map each MPI rank to a device:

```bash
srun /path/to/build_cuda/src/opalx example.in \
  --info 2 --kokkos-map-device-id-by=mpi_rank
```

## What to check

- The startup banner identifies the build and execution backend.
- Parser errors name the statement and location that could not be read.
- Statistics and particle outputs depend on the input-file options and output
  commands.
- A nonzero exit status means the run did not complete successfully.

The [regression-test dashboard]({{< meta regression-tests-url >}}) shows which
inputs currently pass. Input-file compatibility is still being cataloged, so a
regression input is safer than copying an example from the historical OPAL
manual. Continue with the three complete [Worked Input Files](worked-inputs.qmd)
for progressively more detailed starting points.

:::: {.feature-opalx}

## Convert OPAL, ASTRA and Elegant inputs {#sec-toopalx}

`toOPALX.py` converts supported OPAL, ASTRA and Elegant input files into
OPALX inputs. It prepares the input and its companion files,
but does not run a simulation.


::: {.callout-important}

The purpose is **to help** in converting
and not to prepare a bullet-proved input file.

:::

### Download and requirements

[Download toOPALX.py, version 1.4.2](downloads/toOPALX.py){download="toOPALX.py"}
([SHA-256 checksum](downloads/toOPALX.py.sha256){download="toOPALX.py.sha256"}).
This is the frozen release of 1 November 2026.

The single script requires **Python 3.9 or newer** and uses only the Python
standard library. 

### Prepare the source model

Keep the source entry file, included lattice files, particle data and field
maps in one case directory. References must be literal relative filenames
inside that directory; computed filenames, absolute or escaping references
and symbolic links are rejected. The converter preserves the source files
and copies the dependencies needed by the candidate.

Choose the source format explicitly with `--mode`:

::: {.table-responsive}

| Mode | Required inputs | Main supported scope |
|---|---|---|
| `opal` | An entry `.in` file and its recursive `CALL` includes, particle files and maps | Recognized legacy syntax, beam/distribution/source attachments, supported elements and guarded PSI ring/RF placement rules. Unknown commands and explicitly blocked settings stop conversion. |
| `astra` | An ASTRA input, an injected equal-weight electron snapshot with a common clock, and referenced maps | Straight RF/solenoid/quadrupole models with circular apertures, plus restricted single-plane dipole-only beamlines. Cathode emission and arbitrary mixed lattices are outside this release. |
| `elegant` | A supported `.ele` command file, a literal `.lte` lattice and one counted SDDS1 ASCII particle page | One injected electron bunch and one pass through supported drifts, aligned quadrupoles, markers, zero-gap/zero-edge sector bends and restricted standing-wave RFCA models. Binary or multipage SDDS, RPN and general Elegant workflows are unsupported. |

:::

::: {.callout-important}
ASTRA and Elegant conversions always write `FIELDSOLVER, TYPE=NONE`, even
when the source enables space charge. OPAL conversions retain the source
solver settings. Review the solver and boundary conditions before using a
converted input for a space-charge study.
:::

The element list and its restrictions are available directly from the frozen
script. For example:

```bash
python3 toOPALX.py --help --more --mode opal
python3 toOPALX.py --help --more --mode astra
python3 toOPALX.py --help --more --mode elegant
```

### Convert an input

Save the downloaded script beside your case directories. Create a separate
output directory, then use the command for your source format:

```bash
mkdir -p converted

python3 toOPALX.py --mode opal \
  --infile opal-case/lattice.in --outfile converted/opal.in

python3 toOPALX.py --mode astra \
  --infile astra-case/model.in --outfile converted/astra.in

python3 toOPALX.py --mode elegant \
  --infile elegant-case/run.ele --outfile converted/elegant.in
```

Replace the example filenames with your own. The output parent directory
must exist. The output entry file, companion directory and report must all be
new; existing destinations are never overwritten. Use a new output name or
directory for each attempt.

To inspect an OPAL case without writing files:

```bash
python3 toOPALX.py --mode opal --infile opal-case/lattice.in --inspect
```

Inspection prints diagnostic JSON and returns a nonzero status for an
unsupported case. Normal conversion prints a short status and the output and
report filenames. Add `--json` to a conversion command when a script needs
the full report on stdout. Unsupported input or invalid arguments return
status `2`; a completed conversion returns `0`, including cases that require
review. No candidate is published after a refused conversion.

### Output files and the conversion report

For `--outfile converted/opal.in`, keep these outputs together in `converted/`:

::: {.table-responsive}

| Output | Contents |
|---|---|
| `opal.in` | Candidate OPALX entry file. |
| `opal.in.assets/` | Copied maps, particle files, included inputs and companion metadata. Relative references in the candidate point here. |
| `opal.in.report.json` | Complete conversion report, source locations, changes, review notes, approximations, dependency relocation and output fingerprints. |

:::

The full JSON report is saved even when terminal JSON is suppressed. The
asterisk-framed terminal summary highlights drift replacements, model
approximations, particle-file changes and cyclotron placement warnings.
Check the report's `status`, `unavailable_elements`, `model_approximations`,
`asset_migrations`, `placement_warnings` and backend review notes.

### Model changes and current limits

Conversion can change the model. In particular:

- Some element types outside the verified converter scope become drifts when
  their length and placement can be retained. Their fields, kicks or other
  interactions are omitted; every replacement is reported. A drift
  replacement is not an implementation of the original element.
- Legacy `SELECT` and particle-matter declarations/attachments are removed.
  Their interaction physics is not retained. Gas stripping and `UNDULATOR`
  remain unsupported.
- A legacy `BINOMIAL` distribution becomes `GAUSS` with a reported
  approximation. Its binomial shape exponents are removed, while other width
  and correlation expressions are retained without rescaling. Tails and
  higher moments are not preserved.
- SBEND `DESIGNENERGY` and nonzero or unproved `E1/E2` remain rejected.
  Provably zero faces can be omitted. Newer RBEND features do not provide a
  general replacement for these sector-bend settings.
- PSI cyclotron sector expansion and RF-gap placement require review of the
  common centre, map orientation, seams and RF poses. Legacy initial
  conditions and RF timing still need migration; retained report metadata
  does not configure those settings in OPALX. Native single-gap tracking is
  currently limited to one unpolarized positive proton in one container on
  one MPI rank, with `FIELDSOLVER, TYPE=NONE` and no restart. See the
  [cyclotron gap model](../user-guide/cyclotron.qmd#accelerated-beam).

A `review-required` result therefore needs checking before tracking. Compare
particle species, charge, population, units and source coordinates; then
check field strengths, map orientation, geometry, RF phase/timing and solver
settings. Retain the original code's results or another trusted reference
for a numerical comparison. A successful conversion alone is not a regression
test pass, and references or tolerances should not be changed merely to make
the comparison pass.

After that review, launch OPALX from the output directory so its relative
asset references resolve. For the OPAL example, using the executable set in
[the regression smoke test](#regression-smoke-test):

```bash
cd converted
"$OPALX_EXE" opal.in --info 2
```
